description: FortiSASE cloud-delivered SWG enforces web filtering for remote and branch users through FortiGate NGFW policies in the cloud. Trending blocked categories and rules identifies policy drift and shadow IT.
value: Security teams trend FortiSASE web policy violations by FortiGuard category, detecting active threat campaigns, proxy avoidance attempts from users trying to bypass the SWG, and repeat policy violators requiring escalation.
implementation: Forward FortiSASE logs via syslog to Splunk HF. The `TA-fortinet_fortigate` parses FortiSASE traffic identically to on-prem FortiGate. Alert when daily blocks exceed 2× 7-day baseline. Segment by FortiSASE PoP region for regional policy analysis.
visualization: Bar chart (blocks by category), Table (top blocked users), Line chart (daily block trend), Pie chart (category distribution).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Vulnerability scanner signature matches** — Qualys/Tenable traffic triggers IPS/threat signatures for 'FortiSASE SWG Policy Violation Trends (Fortinet)'. Compare `src` against `scanner_ips` lookup.

2. **Policy push during change window** — New deny rule generates expected blocks. Match firewall commit timestamp in change calendar.

3. **Encrypted traffic inspection gap** — TLS-heavy apps bypass deep inspection; volume drop is operational, not a sensor failure.

4. **Red-team C2 simulation** — Approved exercise from `pen_test_hosts.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `src`, `signature_id`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Fortinet FortiSASE web filtering logs in `index=fortisase` with `sourcetype=fortisase:webfilter`. FortiSASE sends logs via FortiAnalyzer or direct syslog. Key fields: `action` (passthrough/blocked/warning), `catdesc` (URL category description), `url`, `user`, `srcip`, `sentbyte`, `rcvdbyte`, `devname` (FortiSASE instance).
• FortiSASE combines FortiGate NGFW capabilities with cloud-delivered SWG, ZTNA, and CASB. Web filtering uses FortiGuard URL categorization with 90+ categories.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure FortiSASE log forwarding: FortiSASE Admin > Log Settings > Remote Logging > Syslog > add Splunk HF.

Verify:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype="fortisase:webfilter" earliest=-1h
| stats count by action
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Policy violation trends:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype="fortisase:webfilter" action=blocked earliest=-7d
| timechart span=1d count by catdesc limit=10
```

Understanding this SPL: Trends blocked web categories over 7 days using FortiGuard categorization. FortiSASE categories include: Malicious Websites, Phishing, Spam URLs, Proxy Avoidance, and custom categories. A spike in 'Proxy Avoidance' means users are actively trying to bypass the SWG — a security concern.

Top violators:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype="fortisase:webfilter" action=blocked earliest=-7d
| stats count dc(url) as unique_urls by user, catdesc
| sort - count
| head 20
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) Visit a known-blocked URL category. Verify the block event.
(b) In FortiSASE: Log & Report > Web Filter.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Block trend by category. Row 2 — Top violating users. Row 3 — Proxy avoidance attempts.
Alert: When Proxy Avoidance blocks exceed baseline by 2x.

Runbook:
1. **Proxy Avoidance spike** — Users trying to bypass SWG. Block the avoidance tools and educate.
2. **Malicious URL spike** — Active threat campaign. Check FortiGuard threat intel.
3. **Repeat violator** — HR notification for policy enforcement.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No web filter events** — FortiSASE log forwarding may not be enabled for web filter.
• **All traffic 'passthrough'** — Web filtering profile may be in monitor-only mode.
grandmaExplanation: FortiSASE filters which websites our employees can visit. We track which blocked categories spike over time — when many people suddenly hit malicious sites, there is likely an attack campaign. We also watch for employees trying to use tools to get around the filter.
hardware: FortiSASE (cloud), FortiClient (endpoint agent), FortiGate (on-prem with SASE integration)
